blocks.text:
One of the most atmospheric parts of the Amazon programme takes place by canoe. The igapó is a flooded forest: water stands between the tree trunks, there are no usual paths, and the boat glides beneath the canopy. Piranha fishing is included in this outing.

After dinner, a night walk with torches begins. By day, the forest is full of greenery and birdsong; at night, it changes completely. Your guide looks for Tinga and Açú caimans by the light reflected in their eyes. With luck, you may also see nightjars, snakes and frogs. Darkness makes even a short trip along the bank an adventure of its own: you hear most animals before you spot them.

blocks.text:
If you have a daytime transfer, you can add a trip to the meeting of the Rio Negro and Solimões rivers. The dark and light waters flow side by side for several kilometres. The difference is apparent in their temperature as well as their colour. From the boat, you can see the distinct boundary between the currents particularly clearly.

Another optional experience is an encounter with Amazonian pink river dolphins. On this excursion, you can see them close up in the water, learn about these river mammals, feed them and have your photograph taken with them. Younger animals are usually darker, while adults gradually develop a pinker colour. In the murky river water, a dolphin can disappear in a second and suddenly reappear right beside you.
